title: Evaluation study to measure the cardiovascular risk of psoriasis patients and patients with atopic dermatitis in dermatological rehabilitation
summary:
As part of a prospective study, the progression of cardiovascular risk in patients with psoriasis and atopic dermatitis will be observed during a dermatological rehabilitation program. This will involve taking a medical history, conducting initial examinations, and administering questionnaires for 50 patients diagnosed with psoriasis vulgaris and 50 patients diagnosed with atopic dermatitis. Additionally, the impact of the disease on quality of life and the levels of anxiety and depression will be measured. The attending physician will provide information on the day of admission. The project consists of a total of four visits. For participants, the first visit will take place on the day of admission, the second visit on the day of discharge, while visits 3 and 4 will be conducted as phone visits at three and six months post-discharge, respectively.

During the first two visits, in addition to a detailed medical history, specific questionnaires related to the activity of the skin disease and cardiovascular risk (ESC SCORE2/SCORE2-OP, SCORE2-Diabetes) will be administered. The examinations will include blood pressure, pulse, weight, waist circumference, and BMI of the patient. The patient will also be questioned about their alcohol and nicotine consumption. As part of the regular rehabilitation program, two blood samples will be taken, and their results will be included in the study. The patient will receive various questionnaires regarding quality of life, disease activity of psoriasis or atopic dermatitis, and the severity of itching. In collaboration with the cardiology department of the Bad Bentheim clinic, a monitored ergometer training program will be conducted. This training will be supplemented with personalized training advice during the second visit.

Appointments for visits 3 and 4 will be scheduled during the discharge consultation. The phone calls will take place three and six months after discharge, respectively. The content of the phone visits will include weight, alcohol and nicotine consumption, the patient's physical activity, and their assessment of disease activity. The primary outcome criterion of the study is an improvement in exercise performance on the cycle ergometer on the day of discharge compared to the day of admission. Additionally, a positive change in specific blood values related to cardiovascular risk factors will be assessed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of atopic dermatitis or diagnosis of psoriasis
Exclusion criteria:
No inclusion of patients who, in the opinion of the enrolling physician, are unable to complete the questionnaires accurately and truthfully.
No inclusion of individuals dependent on the sponsor, study director, or responsible physician.
Individuals who are unable to provide consent are excluded from participation in the study.
